hero.role: I am a robotics engineer specialising in autonomous systems — perception, navigation and control, working together to finish a mission.
hero.where: Mechanical + Electrical Engineering · KAIST, Daejeon · Robotics research intern at the FAIR Lab

now.heading: Currently
now.fair_body: Relay robots working in tandem over a mesh network, plus porting the lab’s stack from ROS 1 to ROS 2.
now.rbnx_body: A mecanum-wheeled CTF robot, autonomous for the first 45 seconds. I designed and created the robot’s URDF, built the simulation in Gazebo using ROS, and raised ₩6,000,000 in funding for the project.
facts: KAIST — Mechanical + Electrical Engineering, expected Feb 2029
KAIST Ambassador — presented KAIST back home in Saudi Arabia

robonexus.title: ROBONEXUS
robonexus.text: A mecanum-wheeled robot for a capture-the-flag competition: collect flags, cross a barrier through a 600 mm gate, deliver them — the first 45 seconds with no driver. I designed the machine, built the simulation, and trained the flag detector on 5,001 synthetic renders because no footage of the venue exists.

drone.title: Autonomous drone
drone.text: A quadrotor that flies a whole mission alone: read a riddle, hand it to a language model, pick the gate the answer points to, avoid what is in the way, then find one storefront from the air and land on it. Knowing its own altitude turned out to be the hard part.

car.title: Self-driving racing car
car.text: A Raspberry Pi car I built end to end. It follows a white line to the grid under a convolutional network, waits for the lights, then hands over to a PID loop on ultrasonic range to race a walled circuit. Two control paradigms, one vehicle, swapping mid-run.

caricature.title: Caricature drawing robot
caricature.text: A dead 3D printer stripped for its steppers and rebuilt as a plotter that draws your face back at you. The interesting part is between the photo and the pen: the portrait becomes a graph, and Dijkstra orders the strokes so the pen spends its time drawing instead of travelling.

ankara.lede: One semester at Middle East Technical University, in a language and a city I did not know.

personal.heading: Off the clock
paragraphs: I game, and I run the servers I game on — which is where the networking and Linux on my skills list actually came from. Nothing teaches you DNS and port forwarding like a friend saying they can’t connect.

I cook, a lot. I like bikes. And I am genuinely interested in the business side of engineering, not just the build — writing the ROBONEXUS proposal and walking away with ₩6,000,000 was one of the more satisfying things I have done, and it was not a technical problem.

contact.heading: Get in touch
contact.lede: I am looking for robotics internships and research positions — perception, navigation and autonomy on real hardware. If you have something running in the field, I would like to hear about it.
